title: The Cash ISA Cut Is Cancelled… And Your £20,000 Just Got More Valuable 😮🏦 #shorts
description:
The cash ISA cut is cancelled: the limit stays at £20,000, and the same Budget made that tax-free room worth more.

What changed: Budget 2025 planned to cut the cash ISA limit to £12,000 a year for savers under 65 from April 2027 (65 and over would keep £20,000), within the overall £20,000 ISA limit. That's £8,000 a year less tax-free cash room (£20,000 − £12,000). Budget 2026 (28 October) scraps the cut: the cash ISA limit stays at £20,000 for all savers over 18 from April 2027. The government will also explore a new incentive for people investing in a stocks and shares ISA for the first time.

The strange part: the same Budget raises the tax rates on savings interest outside ISAs from 6 April 2027: basic rate 24% (now 20%), higher rate 44% (now 40%), additional rate 49% (now 45%). Interest inside an ISA stays tax-free. Most basic-rate savers still pay nothing on their first £1,000 of interest a year (£500 for higher rate) thanks to the Personal Savings Allowance.

Correction: our video 019 said under-65s would get £12,000 in a cash ISA from April 2027. That cut has now been cancelled.

Sources: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/budget-2026-document/budget-2026-html (section 3.9) · https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/budget-2026-overview-of-tax-legislation-and-rates-ootlar/budget-2026-overview-of-tax-legislation-and-rates-ootlar (2.5 and 1.1) · https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/budget-2025-overview-of-tax-legislation-and-rates-ootlar/budget-2025-overview-of-tax-legislation-and-rates-ootlar (2.3) · https://www.gov.uk/individual-savings-accounts

'Raised the tax on savings interest' refers to the savings rates (24%/44%/49% from 6 April 2027); the Personal Savings Allowance (£1,000 basic, £500 higher) and £5,000 starting rate for savings remain, so many savers pay nothing.
